ip_top_stories.title: GEMA Wins Landmark German Court Ruling Against AI Music Startup Suno
ip_top_stories.summary: Germany's Munich Regional Court ruled that AI music generator Suno illegally trained its model on copyrighted songs, delivering a significant win for music rights holders. The court rejected Suno's fair use defence, marking Europe's first major AI music copyright ruling. German performing rights society GEMA brought the case, which has broad implications for how AI companies may train on protected content.

ip_top_stories.title: Reddit's US claims against Perplexity AI, scraper survive under broad DMCA reading
ip_top_stories.summary: A US court allowed Reddit's copyright claims against Perplexity AI to proceed, applying a broad reading of the DMCA to web scraping activity. The ruling is a significant procedural win for Reddit in its ongoing dispute over unauthorised use of its data for AI training. The case is closely watched as a test of how existing copyright law applies to AI data scraping.

ip_top_stories.title: Why AI companies are buying millions of books to destroy them
ip_top_stories.summary: AI companies are purchasing physical books in bulk and destroying them as a method of acquiring training data, exploiting a legal grey area that may sidestep digital copyright restrictions. The practice raises significant questions about the adequacy of existing copyright frameworks to protect authors and publishers. The article examines the legal and ethical implications of this emerging training data acquisition strategy.

ip_top_stories.title: Pippa Bets Artist Royalties Can Solve AI's Copyright War
ip_top_stories.summary: Licensing startup Pippa is proposing a royalty-based model as a solution to ongoing disputes between AI companies and rights holders, arguing that structured payments to artists could resolve the AI copyright impasse. The approach positions licensing as an alternative to litigation, drawing on precedents from the music industry. The proposal reflects growing interest in commercial licensing frameworks as courts continue to weigh in on AI training disputes.

ip_top_stories.title: What does the biggest AI copyright payout in history actually change for creatives?
ip_top_stories.summary: This analysis examines the practical impact of a record AI copyright settlement on creators, questioning whether financial payouts translate into meaningful structural change for rights holders. The piece considers what precedent, if any, large settlements set for future disputes between AI developers and creative industries. It draws on perspectives from artists, lawyers, and industry observers.

ip_further_links.title: From 'Daddy Cool' to the Docket: How Latham & Quinn Emanuel are Testing AI Music in Court
ip_further_links.summary: A look at the legal strategies being deployed by major law firms in AI music copyright cases, examining how specific song disputes are shaping broader litigation tactics.

ip_further_links.title: Who Owns the Harvest? AI Training, Fair Dealing, and the Uncharted Limits of Section 52
ip_further_links.summary: A legal analysis exploring how Section 52 fair dealing provisions apply to AI training data use, and where current copyright law may leave rights holders exposed.

ip_further_links.title: Copyright claim over AI-modified Mona Lisa, Statue of Liberty rejected as 'technical, not creative' in Russian court
ip_further_links.summary: A Russian court dismissed copyright claims over AI-modified versions of iconic public domain artworks, ruling the modifications were technical rather than creative in nature.

ip_further_links.title: AI reshapes film production while raising copyright challenges
ip_further_links.summary: An overview of how AI tools are being adopted across film production workflows and the emerging copyright questions this creates for studios and creators.

ip_further_links.title: Protecting Creators: Campaign Against GenAI Regulations
ip_further_links.summary: A campaign advocating for stronger creator protections in response to proposed generative AI regulations is examined, highlighting tensions between rights holders and technology industry lobbying.

ip_further_links.title: [GuestPost] SEP licensing when the patent landscape changes — IPKat
ip_further_links.summary: An IPKat guest post analysing how shifts in the standard essential patent landscape affect licensing obligations and negotiation dynamics.
